parsed.modern: 3: A part may also be free from either of these imitative characters, and laid out in a common simple farm, am. Some of the greatest beauties of nature are to be found in the fields, and attend an ordinary date of cultivation: wood and water may there be exhibited in several forms and dispositions; we may enlarge or divide the inclosures and give them such shapes and boundaries as we please; every one may be an agreeable spot; together, they may compose beautiful views; the arable, the pasture, and the mead, may succeed one another; and now and then a little wild may be intermixed without impropriety; every beauty, in short, which is not unusual in an inclosed country, whether it arise from neglect or improvement, is here in its place.
